new_quiz.q: What is a Static Switch Parameter?
choices: A number in a material that an instance can set to any value
An on or off switch in a material that turns a part of the graph on or off for each instance
A setting that makes a mesh static in the level
A node that switches between two levels
new_quiz.explain: Each Material Instance sets the switch to on or off. The part of the graph behind the switch is then used or left out for that instance.

new_quiz.q: What is a shader permutation?
choices: A copy of a texture at a lower resolution
A list of the parameters of a material
A shader version compiled for one combination of switches
A light that changes its color over time
new_quiz.explain: Every different combination of switch settings needs its own compiled version of the shader. Each of these versions is a shader permutation.

new_quiz.q: Why is a switch cheap for one single instance?
choices: The part that is switched off is left out of its shader
The switch is checked again on every frame
The switch lowers the resolution of the textures
The switch moves the work to the Game thread
new_quiz.explain: A static switch is decided when the shader is compiled. An instance with the switch off does not pay for the nodes behind it.

new_quiz.q: What grows when a master material has too many permutations?
choices: The size of the meshes in the level
The number of lights in the scene
The length of the parameter names
Compile times and memory use
new_quiz.explain: Each permutation must be compiled and kept in memory. Many switches can create many versions of one material.

new_quiz.q: A master material has 3 Static Switch Parameters. How many different combinations of on and off are possible?
new_quiz.explain: Each switch has two states, so 3 switches give 2 times 2 times 2, which is 8 combinations. That is the most permutations these switches can create.

new_quiz.q: What happens to the number of possible combinations when you add one more switch?
choices: It grows by one
It doubles
It stays the same
It is cut in half
new_quiz.explain: The new switch can be on or off for every combination that already exists. That is why you count before you add more switches.

new_quiz.q: Two instances use exactly the same combination of switches. What does this mean for the permutations?
choices: They need two permutations each
They cannot be used in the same level
They turn all switches off
They share one permutation
new_quiz.explain: Unreal compiles another version only for each different combination. Instances that only differ in colors or numbers share one version.

new_quiz.q: Can a Static Switch Parameter be changed while the game runs?
choices: No, it is fixed when the shader is compiled
Yes, on every frame, like a scalar parameter
Yes, but only from the Level Blueprint
Yes, but only once per level
new_quiz.explain: The word static means the choice is made at compile time. Values that must change during play need normal parameters.

new_quiz.q: Which switches do you add to the master material in this quest?
choices: One for collision, one for shadows and one for physics
One for the sun, one for the sky and one for the fog
One for a detail normal, one for emissive and one more of your choice
One for each texture channel
new_quiz.explain: The detail normal and the emissive are parts that not every surface needs. A switch lets each instance decide.

new_quiz.q: Which switch is the best one to remove?
choices: The one that most instances turn on and off in different ways
The one that is not worth its cost, for example because nobody uses it
The one with the shortest name
The one that was added first
new_quiz.explain: Every switch adds possible permutations. A switch that people do not use adds cost and gives nothing back, so it should go.

new_quiz.q: What is a Material Function?
choices: A Blueprint node that changes a material during play
A setting that turns a material into a decal
A copy of a material that only changes parameters
A small piece of material graph saved as its own asset that many materials can use
new_quiz.explain: A Material Function holds a group of nodes as an asset. You place it in a material like one node.

new_quiz.q: What happens when you fix a mistake inside a Material Function?
choices: Every material that uses the function is fixed too
Only the first material that used it is fixed
The materials that use it must be built again by hand
The function is removed from all materials
new_quiz.explain: The materials do not hold a copy of the nodes. They all point to the same function, so one fix reaches all of them.

new_quiz.q: Which kind of node group is a good choice to move into a Material Function?
choices: A group that is used in only one material
A single Constant node
A group of nodes that you would repeat in many materials
The output node of the material
new_quiz.explain: A function saves work when the same nodes are needed again and again. Detail normal blending is such a group.

new_quiz.q: What is detail normal blending in this quest?
choices: Two color textures are mixed by a vertex color
A second normal texture with a higher tiling is combined with the first
A normal texture is turned into a height texture
A normal texture is removed to save memory
new_quiz.explain: The first normal texture gives the large shapes. The second one repeats more often and adds small detail that shows up close.

new_quiz.q: Which node combines the two normal textures?
choices: Lerp
Landscape Layer Blend
WorldAlignedTexture
BlendAngleCorrectedNormals
new_quiz.explain: BlendAngleCorrectedNormals is made for combining a base normal with a detail normal. It keeps the result a correct normal.

new_quiz.q: Why does the detail normal texture use a higher tiling than the first one?
choices: So it repeats more often and adds small detail
So it covers the mesh only once
So it uses less memory
So it changes the Base Color
new_quiz.explain: A higher tiling makes the texture smaller on the surface. Its bumps then read as fine detail on top of the larger shapes.

new_quiz.q: What do you give each input of MF_DetailNormal?
choices: A random value and a color
A lock and a password
A clear name and a default value
A shortcut key and an icon
new_quiz.explain: A clear name tells the user what to connect. A default value lets the function give a useful result even when that input is left empty.

new_quiz.q: Why do you write a description for the function?
choices: The function cannot be saved without one
So other people know what the function does without opening it
The description makes the function faster
So the function gets the prefix MF_
new_quiz.explain: A function is made to be shared. The description tells the next person what it is for, so they can use it with confidence.

new_quiz.q: Why do you use the function in 2 different materials?
choices: A function only compiles when two materials use it
The two materials must look the same
One material holds the inputs and the other the outputs
It shows that the same nodes are now reused and not built twice
new_quiz.explain: Reuse is the point of a function. Two materials that share MF_DetailNormal prove that the group of nodes exists only once.

new_quiz.q: A material shows the detail normal too strongly, and it uses MF_DetailNormal. Where can you fix this for all materials at once?
choices: Inside the Material Function
In the Details panel of each mesh
In the World Settings of the level
In the texture file of the first normal
new_quiz.explain: The blend is built in the function, so that is where a general fix belongs. Every material that uses the function gets the change.

new_quiz.q: What is a vertex of a mesh?
choices: A texture that covers the mesh
A corner point of the mesh
A material slot of the mesh
A copy of the mesh in the level
new_quiz.explain: A mesh is made of triangles, and their corner points are the vertices. Each vertex can store a color.

new_quiz.q: What can you do with the colors stored on the vertices?
choices: Change the collision of the mesh
Make the mesh cast no shadow
Let a material read them and use them to blend two surfaces
Move the mesh while the game runs
new_quiz.explain: A material can read the vertex color. Where you paint, the material shows more of the second surface, such as moss over stone.

new_quiz.q: Which node reads the painted color in the material?
choices: Texture Sample
TexCoord
Constant3Vector
Vertex Color
new_quiz.explain: The Vertex Color node gives the color stored on the vertices of the mesh. Each of its channels can be used as a mask.

new_quiz.q: How do you use the red channel of the Vertex Color node in this quest?
choices: As the Alpha of a Lerp node between the two surfaces
As the Base Color of the material
As the Roughness of the material
As the tiling of the textures
new_quiz.explain: A Lerp node blends from one input to the other by its Alpha. With red as the Alpha, the amount of red paint decides how much of the second surface shows.

new_quiz.q: What does red paint do on a mesh with this material?
choices: It makes the mesh red
It removes the base surface from the material
It puts the second surface over the base surface
It deletes the painted vertices
new_quiz.explain: You do not see the red itself. The material uses it as a mask, so painted areas show the second surface.

new_quiz.q: Why is a sphere a better test mesh than a simple cube?
choices: A sphere has no UVs
The paint is stored on the vertices, and a simple cube has too few
A cube cannot have a material
A sphere is always larger than a cube
new_quiz.explain: You can only paint where there are vertices. A simple cube has just its corners, so there is nothing to paint on its faces.

new_quiz.q: Which editor mode do you use to paint on the mesh?
choices: Landscape Mode
Foliage Mode
Modeling Mode
Mesh Paint mode
new_quiz.explain: Mesh Paint mode paints vertex colors onto meshes in the level. The paint belongs to that one placed mesh.

new_quiz.q: What does a height-based blend use to decide where the second surface appears first?
choices: A height texture
The height of the camera
The Z position of the mesh in the level
The scale of the mesh
new_quiz.explain: The height texture says which parts of the surface are high and which are low. The second surface then appears in some parts before others, for example in the cracks first.

new_quiz.q: What does the height-based blend improve?
choices: The frame rate of the level
The number of vertices of the mesh
The edge of the blend, which looks sharp and natural
The size of the texture files
new_quiz.explain: A plain vertex blend fades softly between the painted vertices. The height texture breaks that fade into a detailed edge.

new_quiz.q: Why is vertex paint a cheap way to add variety to a level?
choices: It lowers the triangle count of each mesh
Copies of one mesh can look different with the same material
It removes the need for textures
It turns off the lighting on painted meshes
new_quiz.explain: The mesh and the material stay the same. Only the paint differs from copy to copy, which breaks up repetition at a low cost.

new_quiz.q: What is Nanite?
choices: The lighting system that calculates bounced light
The tool that paints vertex colors
The editor for building materials
The system in Unreal Engine 5 that lets you use meshes with millions of triangles
new_quiz.explain: Nanite is the geometry system of Unreal Engine 5. It makes very detailed meshes usable in real time.

new_quiz.q: Why can Nanite handle meshes with millions of triangles?
choices: It only draws the detail that the screen can show
It turns every mesh into a flat image
It removes the materials from the mesh
It draws each mesh only on every second frame
new_quiz.explain: Far away, a mesh covers few pixels and needs few triangles. Nanite picks the detail that fits the screen, so the full triangle count is never drawn at once.

new_quiz.q: What is a high-poly mesh?
choices: A mesh that is placed high above the level
A mesh with many material slots
A mesh with a very large number of triangles
A mesh with a very large texture
new_quiz.explain: High-poly means many polygons, which are the triangles of the mesh. Such meshes show the gain of Nanite most clearly.

new_quiz.q: How do you enable Nanite on a mesh in this quest?
choices: Open Edit, then Plugins, and enable Nanite
Open the mesh and tick Enable Nanite Support in its Nanite Settings
Set the Mobility of the mesh to Movable
Add a Nanite component to the level
new_quiz.explain: Nanite is a setting of the mesh asset. You open the mesh and tick Enable Nanite Support in its Nanite Settings.

new_quiz.q: Which Nanite visualization modes do you use to inspect the mesh in the level?
choices: Lit, Unlit and Wireframe
Game, Draw and GPU
Key, Fill and Rim
Triangles, Clusters and Overdraw
new_quiz.explain: These three modes show how Nanite draws the mesh: its triangles, the clusters they are grouped in, and how much is drawn over other geometry.

new_quiz.q: In the Triangles visualization mode, what do you see when you move the camera away from a Nanite mesh?
choices: The mesh is drawn with fewer and larger triangles
The mesh is drawn with more and smaller triangles
The mesh turns into a cube
The mesh keeps exactly the same triangles
new_quiz.explain: Nanite draws only the detail the screen can show. From far away the mesh covers fewer pixels, so fewer triangles are enough.

new_quiz.q: Which kind of material does the quest name as one that Nanite does not support?
choices: Opaque materials
Materials with a normal map
Translucent materials
Materials with parameters
new_quiz.explain: Nanite does not support every kind of material, and translucent ones are an example. You check the list on the documentation page to see which materials of a project are affected.

new_quiz.q: What does displacement do?
choices: It moves the whole mesh to another place in the level
A texture moves the surface of the mesh in and out to add real detail
It replaces the mesh with a simpler one
It swaps the material of the mesh during play
new_quiz.explain: Displacement changes the shape of the surface itself. A normal map only fakes bumps in the lighting.

new_quiz.q: Nanite displacement does not work in your project. What does the quest ask you to do then?
choices: Remove Nanite from all meshes
Install an older engine version
Skip the quest
Write what you would need to enable
new_quiz.explain: Displacement depends on the engine version and the project settings. If it is not available, you find out what is missing and write it down.

new_quiz.q: What do the 3 lines of your writeup say?
choices: Which mesh, which material and which level you used
How many triangles, vertices and textures the mesh has
When you would use Nanite, when you would not, and one cost to watch
Which three visualization modes exist
new_quiz.explain: Nanite changes how many polygons are too many, but it has limits. The writeup shows that you can decide when it fits.

new_quiz.q: Where does the eye of a viewer go first in a picture?
choices: To the darkest corner
To the brightest spot with the most contrast
To the center of the frame
To the largest object
new_quiz.explain: Brightness and contrast pull the eye. Lighting artists use this to lead the viewer to the important place.

new_quiz.q: What is a hero area?
choices: The most important place in a scene, where you want people to look
The place where the player character starts
The area with the most triangles
The area that is lit by the sun
new_quiz.explain: A hero area can be an entrance, a landmark or a focal prop. You light it so that the viewer notices it first.

new_quiz.q: What is the key light?
choices: The light that softens the shadows
The light that comes from behind the subject
The light from the sky
The main light
new_quiz.explain: The key light is the main light on the subject. Its direction sets where the shadows fall.

new_quiz.q: What does the fill light do?
choices: It casts the strongest shadows
It lights the background only
It softens the shadows
It replaces the key light
new_quiz.explain: The fill light adds a little light to the shadow side. The shadows stay, but they are less dark.

new_quiz.q: What does the rim light do?
choices: It comes from behind and separates the subject from the background
It lights the floor in front of the subject
It makes the whole scene brighter
It removes the reflections from the subject
new_quiz.explain: A rim light draws a bright edge around the subject. That edge lifts the subject off the background.

new_quiz.q: What does GI mean?
choices: General intensity, which is the brightness of a light
Global illumination, which is bounced light
Grid index, which is the position of a light
Glow input, which is the emissive of a material
new_quiz.explain: GI is global illumination, the light that bounces from surface to surface. You check it and the reflections with the Lumen visualization modes.

new_quiz.q: Why do you run stat unit before and after you add your lights?
choices: To save the lights to the level
To turn on the Lumen reflections
To switch the lights to physical units
To see how much frame time the extra lights cost
new_quiz.explain: The command stat unit shows how long each frame takes. The difference between the two readings is the cost of your lights.

new_quiz.q: Why do you take the before and after stills through the same Cine Camera Actor?
choices: A Cine Camera makes lights cheaper
The Cine Camera adds the rim light
Both stills then show the same view, so only the lighting differs
The stills are then saved in the level
new_quiz.explain: A fixed camera makes the comparison fair. Any difference you see comes from your lighting and not from a new angle.

new_quiz.q: Why do you ask another person where their eye goes first?
choices: They do not know where they are meant to look, so their answer is an honest test
They must approve the lights before you can save
They can see the stat numbers better
They choose the hero area for you
new_quiz.explain: You already know where the hero area is, so you cannot test it yourself. A fresh viewer shows if the lighting really leads the eye.

new_quiz.q: The person you asked looks at a bright lamp in the corner first, and not at your hero area. What does this tell you?
choices: The camera has the wrong focal length
The corner is brighter or has more contrast than the hero area
The hero area has too many lights
The person did not look long enough
new_quiz.explain: The eye goes to the brightest spot with the most contrast. You dim the corner or strengthen the hero area until the hero area wins.
